meaning: Arrows run from mathematical ingredients to results that use them. This overview is curated from the papers; the Source references view displays the separate compiler-recorded relation.

nodes.title: Source graphs
nodes.summary: Translate a formula into one fixed list of graphs. Satisfiability and unsatisfiability give different colouring guarantees for that same list. Expander existence is upstream of this source theorem, not a third direct input.

nodes.title: Balanced families
nodes.summary: Polynomial families supply the distribution and product estimates needed to select matrix coordinates. This existence and counting theorem remains external to Lean.

nodes.title: Choose the parameters
nodes.summary: Select one numerical schedule and a formula-independent cutoff that make every amplification step admissible.

nodes.title: Construct the matrices
nodes.summary: Build the three preliminary stages, the fourth-stage matrix, and its labelled copies without using a satisfying assignment or the satisfiability of the formula.

nodes.title: Protect the lower bound
nodes.summary: Labelled duplication preserves exact communication cost and gives lower bounds on large restrictions and on a designated reference submatrix.

nodes.title: Align the restriction scales
nodes.summary: An interlace and transpose bring the lower bounds to a common row-density threshold, making them suitable for the next step.

nodes.title: Restore robustness
nodes.summary: A general communication lemma turns the aligned bounds into a robust lower bound for an interlaced matrix. It also transports upper bounds.

nodes.title: Add one bit to the gap
nodes.summary: Combine the construction-specific lower bound and the robustness lemma. One fixed successor gains exactly one bit in the negative case, with a matching upper bound and exact carrier sizes.

nodes.title: Start with the full-cube matrix
nodes.summary: A rank argument gives the initial exact communication cost and the robustness needed to begin amplification.

nodes.title: Repeat the same construction
nodes.summary: Iterate the matrix-and-budget successor k times on each source graph. The matrices are shared by both satisfiability cases.

nodes.title: An exact k-bit gap
nodes.summary: Induction gives a low-cost member when the formula is satisfiable, and exactly the prescribed budget plus k for every member when it is unsatisfiable.

nodes.title: Bound the matrix dimensions
nodes.summary: Read dimensions from the actual successor matrices and bound their logarithms by a scalar recurrence. The fixed cutoff makes the final bound at most floor(n/(2k)).

nodes.title: Count the same matrix's entries
nodes.summary: Convert the logarithmic dimension bound into separate row and column bounds, then multiply. No padding or replacement matrix is used.

nodes.title: Communication gap and size
nodes.summary: For each fixed positive k, sufficiently large formulas yield one nonempty matrix family with the stated satisfiability gap and at most 2^floor(n/k) entries per matrix, conditional on the two stated outside inputs.
